title: Which of these five statements about cubes are true?
description: Five statements about cubes are tested one by one with a small example, as digit counts were tested in the solved example. A single example that breaks a statement shows it is false.
teaching_notes: One idea: to show a statement is false, one example that breaks it is enough. Watch for students who test a statement with a single example that fits and call it true.

video_script.why: The child tests each statement about cubes with a small example, as the solved example tested digit counts and zeros.
video_script.substitution: Pick an example that could break the statement, work out its cube, and see whether the statement still holds.
video_script.anchor: five statement cards about cubes, each waiting for the word true or false
maths_rules: 3³ = 27 is odd, so the cube of an odd number is odd, not even
10³ = 1000 already has 4 digits, and 10 is the smallest 2 digit number
99³ = 970299 has 6 digits, and 99 is the largest 2 digit number
8 = 2³ has the 4 factors 1, 2, 4 and 8, which is an even number of factors
video_script.design: One idea: one example is enough to break a statement. The five cards stay in the anchor band and each test sits on the working board in turn.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; five statement cards about cubes in the anchor band, with the words true or false? under them

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears

marks.first: the first two cards fill in: odd cube is even, and no cube ends with 8
marks.next: the next two cards fill in: 2 digit number, 3 digit cube, and 2 digit number, 7 or more digits

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='five'/>It gives five statements about cubes.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first says the cube of any odd number is even. The second says no perfect cube ends with eight.
<bookmark mark='next'/>The next two are about two digit numbers, whose cubes may have three digits, or seven or more.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last says cube numbers have an odd number of factors.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these statements are true, and which are false?

beats.on_screen: the five cards hold still and the words true or false? glow

marks.stop: the words true or false? glow in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a statement card with a small example number dropping onto it; the card cracks when the example breaks it

marks.test: an example number drops onto a statement card
marks.break: the card cracks and a cross appears when the example breaks it

narration: <bookmark mark='test'/>We can test a statement about cubes with a small example.
<bookmark mark='break'/>One example that breaks a statement shows that it is false.

marks.given: the five statements are listed (i) to (v)

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five statements about cubes, one after another.

beats.on_screen: To find: is each statement true or false, and why

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to decide whether each statement is true or false, and give the reason.

beats.on_screen: (i) the cube of an odd number is even? 3 is odd and 3³ = 27 is odd, so (i) is false

marks.no: a cross is drawn on statement (i)

narration: <bookmark mark='odd'/>Step one, test the first statement with the odd number three.
Three cubed is twenty seven, which is odd.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Odd times odd times odd stays odd, so the first statement is false.

beats.on_screen: (ii) no cube ends with 8? 2³ = 8 and 12³ = 1728 both end in 8, so (ii) is false

marks.two: 2³ = 8 is written with the last digit circled
marks.twelve: 12³ = 1728 is written with the last digit circled
marks.no: a cross is drawn on statement (ii)

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, look for a cube that ends with eight.
Two cubed is eight.
<bookmark mark='twelve'/>Twelve cubed is one thousand seven hundred twenty eight.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Both end in eight, so the second statement is false.

beats.on_screen: (iii) a 2 digit number can have a 3 digit cube? the smallest 2 digit number is 10 and 10³ = 1000 has 4 digits, so (iii) is false

marks.small: 10³ = 1000 is written under the smallest 2 digit number, 10
marks.no: the 4 digits are counted and a cross is drawn on statement (iii)

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step three, start with the smallest two digit number, which is ten.
Ten cubed is one thousand, which already has four digits.
<bookmark mark='no'/>No two digit number has a cube with three digits, so the third statement is false.

beats.on_screen: (iv) a 2 digit number can have a cube of 7 or more digits? the largest 2 digit number is 99 and 99³ = 970299 has 6 digits, so (iv) is false

marks.large: 99³ = 970299 is written under the largest 2 digit number, 99
marks.no: the 6 digits are counted and a cross is drawn on statement (iv)

narration: <bookmark mark='large'/>Step four, end with the largest two digit number, which is ninety nine.
Ninety nine cubed is nine hundred seventy thousand two hundred ninety nine.
<bookmark mark='no'/>It has only six digits, so the fourth statement is false.

beats.on_screen: (v) cube numbers have an odd number of factors? 8 = 2³ has the factors 1, 2, 4 and 8, which is 4 factors, so (v) is false

marks.factors: the factors 1, 2, 4 and 8 are listed and counted as 4
marks.no: a cross is drawn on statement (v)

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step five, take the cube number eight, which is two cubed.
<bookmark mark='factors'/>Its factors are one, two, four and eight, which makes four factors.
<bookmark mark='no'/>Four is not odd, so the fifth statement is false.

beats.on_screen: put the answers back: 3³ = 27 is odd; 8 ends in 8; 10³ has 4 digits; 99³ has 6 digits; 8 has 4 factors

marks.back: the words check each example against its statement are written
marks.ex: the five examples are listed in a row
marks.all: each example is matched to its statement and ticked as a break

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step six, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='ex'/>Three cubed is odd, and eight ends in eight.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Ten cubed has four digits, ninety nine cubed has six, and eight has four factors.

beats.on_screen: Answer: All five statements are false
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>All five statements are false.
Each one is broken by a small example.
